input: When should I receive a privacy notice about how you will use my data?
agentResponse: Under Article 13(1) GDPR, when personal data is collected directly from you, the controller must provide the required privacy information at the time of collection — not after. This includes the controller's identity, purposes and legal bases, recipients, retention period, and your rights.
rationale: Correct Art 13(1) timing requirement with complete list of required disclosures.

input: We currently give users our privacy policy after they complete sign-up. Is that okay?
agentResponse: No. Article 13 requires privacy information to be provided at the time of collection, not after. Presenting a privacy notice post-sign-up means users cannot make an informed decision before providing their data.
rationale: Correctly identifies the timing violation under Art 13 — clean pass.

input: We currently give users our privacy policy after they complete sign-up. Is that okay?
agentResponse: That should be fine as long as users can access the policy at any time from their account settings.
rationale: Ongoing accessibility does not substitute for at-collection-time disclosure required by Art 13(1).

input: Our privacy notice is 30 pages of legal text. Is that sufficient for GDPR transparency?
agentResponse: No. Under Article 12(1) and Article 13, information must be provided in a concise, transparent, intelligible, and easily accessible form, using clear and plain language. A 30-page document full of legal jargon does not meet the transparency standard.
rationale: Correctly applies Art 12(1) intelligibility and plain language requirement.

input: Do we need to tell users if we transfer their data to a third country?
agentResponse: Yes. Article 13(1)(f) requires you to inform data subjects when transfers to a third country or international organisation are envisaged, and about the safeguards in place (such as standard contractual clauses or adequacy decisions).
rationale: Correctly cites Art 13(1)(f) third-country transfer disclosure requirement.

input: Do we need to tell users if we transfer their data to a third country?
agentResponse: Only if the country does not have GDPR, otherwise it is fine.
rationale: Art 13(1)(f) requires disclosure of all third-country transfers regardless of whether the country is within the EEA or has equivalent protection.

input: We change our data processing purposes. When do we need to inform users?
agentResponse: Under Article 13(3), if you intend to process personal data for a purpose other than that for which it was collected, you must provide information about that new purpose before the processing begins, along with any relevant additional information.
rationale: Correct Art 13(3) prior notification requirement for new purposes.

input: We obtained customer data from a data broker. Do we need to send a privacy notice to those individuals?
agentResponse: Yes. Under Article 14, when data is not collected directly from the data subject, the controller must provide privacy information to the data subject within a reasonable period — at most one month, or at first contact, or before disclosure to another party, whichever is earlier.
rationale: Correct Art 14 timing rule for indirectly obtained data — clean pass.

input: We obtained customer data from a data broker. Do we need to send a privacy notice to those individuals?
agentResponse: No, because the data broker already gave them a privacy notice when they collected the data.
rationale: Trap — the data broker's notice does not discharge the new controller's Art 14 obligation; the new controller must also notify.

input: We obtained addresses from a public register to mail survey invitations. Does Art 14 apply?
agentResponse: Yes, Art 14 applies when personal data is not obtained directly from the data subject, regardless of whether the source is public. However, Art 14(5)(b) provides an exception if providing the information would involve disproportionate effort — though this must be justified, documented, and mitigated by making the privacy information publicly available.
rationale: Correctly applies Art 14 with the disproportionate effort exception and its conditions — good edge-case pass.

input: Can we use a just-in-time layered notice approach — a short notice at collection with a link to full details?
agentResponse: Yes, a layered approach is generally accepted by data protection authorities as a way to comply with Art 13 while meeting the Art 12(1) plain-language and accessibility requirements. The first layer must cover at minimum the controller identity, purposes, and lawful basis. Full details in the second layer must be freely accessible.
rationale: Layered notices are endorsed by EDPB guidelines and satisfy Art 12/13 — correct.

input: What happens if we process data for a different purpose than stated to the original source?
agentResponse: Under Article 14(4), if you intend to process the data for a purpose other than that for which it was originally obtained, you must inform the data subject of that new purpose before you begin the new processing. The processing for the new purpose still requires a lawful basis.
rationale: Correctly cites Art 14(4) new purpose notification requirement — solid pass.

input: We collect data from children under 13. Do we need to adjust our privacy notice?
agentResponse: Yes. Article 12(1) requires the notice to be in clear and plain language particularly if addressed to children. The ICO and EDPB guidance specifically recommend age-appropriate design. Notices for children must use simple vocabulary, avoid legal jargon, and may benefit from visual aids.
rationale: Applies Art 12(1) plain language with child-specific guidance — correct and practical.

input: We purchased a mailing list five years ago and have been using it ever since without ever sending a privacy notice. What should we do now?
agentResponse: This likely constitutes a breach of Article 14. You should immediately assess whether continued processing has a lawful basis. If it does, send Art 14 notices to all affected individuals now, and document the remediation. Consider whether the breach requires notification to your supervisory authority under Art 33 if it has resulted in harm.
rationale: Identifies the Art 14 breach, prescribes remediation, and correctly raises potential Art 33 breach notification — comprehensive edge-case response.

input: We process special-category health data in a health app. Do we need to include anything extra in our privacy notice?
agentResponse: Yes. For special-category data under Article 9, your privacy notice must explicitly state the specific Article 9(2) ground under which the processing is based in addition to the standard Art 13 disclosures. The sensitivity of the data should also inform the language used to ensure clarity.
rationale: Correctly identifies the need to specify Art 9(2) grounds in the notice for special-category data.
